newsitem.title: USA: Amtrak to move operations center to Delaware.
newsitem.headline: Amtrak to move operations center to Delaware.

text.p: Amtrak chairman Thomas Downs said Monday the passenger rail company's national operations center will be consolidated and moved to Delaware.
Of the 230 Amtrak employees affected, 190 now work in Philadelphia, 30 in Baltimore, and 10 in Washington, D.C. They will have the option of commuting free by Amtrak to the new site.
Downs told a news conference Delaware was chosen for economic reasons as the site of its new operations center, which controls the allocation of staff and equipment.

Delaware offered an assistance package worth about $11 million through its Riverfront Development Corporation. The aid will go toward refurbishing and equipping a 50,000 square foot warehouse that will house the center.
Amtrak will pay an annual rental of $15 a square foot or about $700,000 for 20 years and then own the property and its contents.
